CVE-2026-62313.title: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Prior to ...
CVE-2026-62313.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Prior to version 7.3.0, project-level enforcement of `restricted.containers.privilege=isolated` can be trivially bypassed, allowing a user to create a non-isolated (shared host idmap) container in a project that is configured to forbid them. The restriction only rejects an explicitly set `security.idmap.isolated=false` (or empty) and fails to enforce anything when the key is omitted entirely. Because an unset `security.idmap.isolated` defaults to `false` (non-isolation), a user simply leaves the key out and obtains exactly the container state the restriction is meant to forbid. This defeats the tenant-isolation guarantee the restriction exists to provide. Containers in the project share the host uid/gid map instead of receiving unique, non-overlapping ranges, weakening the isolation boundary between co-tenant containers and the host. Version 7.3.0 patches the issue.

CVE-2026-81501.title: Restricted client can import a private image from another project
CVE-2026-81501.description: ### Summary A project-restricted TLS client that cannot `GET /1.0/images/{fingerprint}` for a **private** image in another project can still import that same fingerprint into their own project. `imageDownload` reuses any matching local image via `GetImageFromAnyProject` without checking `Public` or `CanView`. Image blobs are stored globally under `var/images/<fingerprint>`, so the caller receives the private image properties and files. This is the image-object counterpart of GHSA-c9f5-j9c3-mhrg (instance copy from `req.Source.Project` without `CanView`). It is not a privileged-container escape. ### Affected - Runtime reproduction: Ubuntu 24.04 package **Incus 6.0.0** (`6.0.0-1ubuntu0.3`) in an isolated Docker environment. - Same unguarded call is present on `lxc/incus` at `v7.3.0-432-gf216a6d46` in `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go`. - Full release range should be confirmed by maintainers. ### Contrast (same restricted client, same fingerprint) | Request | Result | | --- | --- | | `GET /1.0/images/<fp>?project=default` | **404** (`imageGet` requires `CanView` or public/secret) | | `POST /1.0/images?project=hunt-b` with `source.type=image` pulling from an attacker HTTPS server that only echoes `<fp>` | operation **Success**; image now listed in `hunt-b` with the victim `properties` | The attacker server never supplies image bytes. Incus clones the local private record and files. A harmless marker (`INCUS-HUNT-MARKER`) in the victim image properties appears in the attacker project. ### Impact A restricted client with `CanCreateImages` (or the ability to create an instance from an image) in their own project, who already knows a private image fingerprint from another project, can: - copy that image's properties and global blob into their project; - then view, export, or launch instances from it inside their project. This breaks Incus project isolation for private images. **Limitation:** the 64-hex fingerprint is not returned by `GET` / list to a caller without `CanView`. The attacker must obtain it out of band (logs, backups, a former project membership, a predictable custom image, etc.). No victim interaction is required after that. ### Root cause `imageGet` / `imagesGet` / `imageExport` apply `CheckPermission(ObjectImage, CanView)` and hide private images behind 404. `imageDownload`, after a dest-project miss, does: ```go _, imgInfo, err = tx.GetImageFromAnyProject(ctx, fp) // then CreateImage into the caller project — no Public / CanView check ``` Reachable from: - `POST /1.0/images` with `source.type=image` - `POST /1.0/instances` when `source.server != ''` `AllowImageDownload` only enforces `restricted.images.servers` (remote host allowlist). It is not an object-level `CanView` check. ### Suggested fix After `GetImageFromAnyProject` succeeds, only reuse the local image if: 1. `imgInfo.Public` is true, or 2. `CheckPermission` on `ObjectImage(imgInfo.Project, fingerprint)` with `EntitlementCanView` succeeds. Otherwise continue with a real remote download. Do not copy the private local image. ### Dedup Not a duplicate of: - GHSA-mq9x-prm8-3vpw / GHSA-c9f5-j9c3-mhrg — instance copy `Source.Project` without `CanView` (same class, different object and entry point) - GHSA-p8mm-23gg-jc9r — simplestreams concatenated fingerprint - GHSA-f6m5-xw2g-xc4x / GHSA-p2v3-6wvc-cv3p — fingerprint used as a filesystem path - GHSA-8gw4-p4wq-4hcv — URL import HEAD SSRF - Incus 7.3 leftover name-as-path / OpenRoot issues ### PoC Isolated Docker environment attached as `incus-private-image-anyproject.zip`. ```bash unzip incus-private-image-anyproject.zip cd incus-private-image-anyproject ./run.sh ``` Expected: `all_checks_passed: true`, `verdict=private_image_cross_project_reuse_reproduced_at_runtime`. The container starts Ubuntu 24.04 + distro Incus 6.0.0, creates a private image in `default` (marker in `properties.description`), a project `hunt-b`, and a restricted TLS cert bound only to `hunt-b`. It then runs the contrast above. Harmless marker only; no instance is launched. `results/runtime.json` from our run is included. ### Severity Medium. Suggested: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N` = 6.3. | Metric | Value | Reason | | --- | --- | --- | | AV | N | HTTPS API | | AC | H | 64-hex fingerprint required; not enumerable via GET/list (404) | | PR | L | project-restricted TLS client with image-create rights, not admin | | UI | N | no victim interaction | | S | C | breaks project isolation (same Scope as GHSA-c9f5) | | C | H | full private image (properties + rootfs blob) | | I | N | victim image is not modified | | A | N | no availability impact | If maintainers treat fingerprint knowledge like instance-name knowledge in GHSA-c9f5, the matching vector is `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N` = 7.7. I am reporting 6.3. ### Credit Yuliang Xiao

Image blobs are stored globally under `var/images/<fingerprint>`, so the caller receives the private image properties and files. This is the image-object counterpart of GHSA-c9f5-j9c3-mhrg (instance copy from `req.Source.Project` without `CanView`). It is not a privileged-container escape. ### Affected - Runtime reproduction: Ubuntu 24.04 package **Incus 6.0.0** (`6.0.0-1ubuntu0.3`) in an isolated Docker environment. - Same unguarded call is present on `lxc/incus` at `v7.3.0-432-gf216a6d46` in `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go`. - Full release range should be confirmed by maintainers. ### Contrast (same restricted client, same fingerprint) | Request | Result | | --- | --- | | `GET /1.0/images/<fp>?project=default` | **404** (`imageGet` requires `CanView` or public/secret) | | `POST /1.0/images?project=hunt-b` with `source.type=image` pulling from an attacker HTTPS server that only echoes `<fp>` | operation **Success**; image now listed in `hunt-b` with the victim `properties` | The attacker server never supplies image bytes. Incus clones the local private record and files. A harmless marker (`INCUS-HUNT-MARKER`) in the victim image properties appears in the attacker project. ### Impact A restricted client with `CanCreateImages` (or the ability to create an instance from an image) in their own project, who already knows a private image fingerprint from another project, can: - copy that image's properties and global blob into their project; - then view, export, or launch instances from it inside their project. This breaks Incus project isolation for private images. **Limitation:** the 64-hex fingerprint is not returned by `GET` / list to a caller without `CanView`. The attacker must obtain it out of band (logs, backups, a former project membership, a predictable custom image, etc.). No victim interaction is required after that. ### Root cause `imageGet` / `imagesGet` / `imageExport` apply `CheckPermission(ObjectImage, CanView)` and hide private images behind 404. `imageDownload`, after a dest-project miss, does: ```go _, imgInfo, err = tx.GetImageFromAnyProject(ctx, fp) // then CreateImage into the caller project — no Public / CanView check ``` Reachable from: - `POST /1.0/images` with `source.type=image` - `POST /1.0/instances` when `source.server != ''` `AllowImageDownload` only enforces `restricted.images.servers` (remote host allowlist). It is not an object-level `CanView` check. ### Suggested fix After `GetImageFromAnyProject` succeeds, only reuse the local image if: 1. `imgInfo.Public` is true, or 2. `CheckPermission` on `ObjectImage(imgInfo.Project, fingerprint)` with `EntitlementCanView` succeeds. Otherwise continue with a real remote download. It then runs the contrast above. Harmless marker only; no instance is launched. `results/runtime.json` from our run is included. ### Severity Medium. CVE-2026-62313.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Prior to version 7.3.0, project-level enforcement of `restricted.containers.privilege=isolated` can be trivially bypassed, allowing a user to create a non-isolated (shared host idmap) container in a project that is configured to forbid them. The restriction only rejects an explicitly set `security.idmap.isolated=false` (or empty) and fails to enforce anything when the key is omitted entirely. Because an unset `security.idmap.isolated` defaults to `false` (non-isolation), a user simply leaves the key out and obtains exactly the container state the restriction is meant to forbid. This defeats the tenant-isolation guarantee the restriction exists to provide. Containers in the project share the host uid/gid map instead of receiving unique, non-overlapping ranges, weakening the isolation boundary between co-tenant containers and the host. Version 7.3.0 patches the issue.
